# Model card: chargeback risk — logistic regression

<!-- Generated by `cbp evaluate`. Synthetic data only; do not edit by hand. -->

## Model details

- **Model:** Logistic regression (`logreg`), chargeback-prediction v1.0.0.
- **Output:** calibrated probability that a card-not-present charge is disputed within the network dispute window; 30 point-in-time features (see [features.md](../features.md)).
- **Selection:** lowest test-window cost under the expected-cost blocking rule, ahead of gradient boosting.
- **Explanations:** exact SHAP values per prediction, served by `/v1/explain`.
- **License:** MIT. **Contact:** repository issues.

## Intended use

- Rank recurring and one-off card-not-present charges by dispute risk **before** they are submitted, so a merchant can skip, step-up, remind or review the riskiest.
- Feed the per-amount expected-cost rule, which needs calibrated probabilities.
- Prioritise representment effort and evidence gathering once a dispute lands.

**Out of scope:** authorisation-time fraud decisions for card-present traffic; credit or eligibility decisions about people; use on real data without retraining and re-evaluation; any automated action without a human-reviewable reason (the SHAP factors and rationale exist for that).

## Training and evaluation data

Fully **synthetic** customers, subscriptions, charges and disputes from this repository's generator, with planted friendly-fraud and stolen-card patterns. No real cardholder or merchant data was used.

| Window | Charges | Disputes | Rate | Dates |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| train | 12,886 | 242 | 1.9% | 2025-01-01 → 2025-07-25 |
| test | 7,013 | 167 | 2.4% | 2025-11-22 → 2026-02-24 |

Time-based split with a 120-day label gap, so every training label was final before the first test charge.

## Metrics (test window)

| Metric | Value (95% CI where shown) |
|---|---|
| PR-AUC | 0.345 [0.269, 0.431] (random: 0.024) |
| Precision / recall at top 0.5% | 68.6% / 14.4% |
| Precision / recall at top 1.0% | 71.4% / 29.9% |
| Precision / recall at top 5.0% | 22.5% / 47.3% |
| Brier score | 0.0179 |
| Expected calibration error | 0.0137 |
| Saved per 1k charges (expected-cost rule) | $611 [$360, $850] |
| Share of achievable saving | 24.9% |
| Charges blocked | 82 (1.2%), of which 27 false declines |
| Residual dispute ratio | 1.6% (approve-all: 2.4%) |

Full tables, the cost assumptions and the sensitivity analysis are in [the cost report](report.md).

## Limitations

- **Synthetic data.** The planted signals are cleaner and more monotone than real traffic; absolute numbers say nothing about production performance.
- **Few positives.** The test window holds only 167 disputes; read the intervals, not the point estimates.
- **Label delay.** Disputes arrive weeks to months after the charge, so live monitoring of precision lags by the dispute window; track score distribution drift and calibration on matured cohorts instead.
- **Where it is weakest:** charges that look entirely normal. The lowest-scored bin has an observed dispute rate of 3.6% against 0.2% predicted; no behavioural feature separates them.
- **Costs are assumptions.** The expected-cost rule is only as good as the unit economics fed to it; the sensitivity table shows how the decision shifts.

## Ethical considerations

- **False declines land on legitimate customers.** Prefer soft actions (reminders, step-up) over hard declines, and keep a human-reviewable reason for every block.
- **Proxy features.** No protected attributes are used, but geography (IP/BIN country mismatch) and email domain can correlate with them. Before production use, audit block and false-decline rates across regions and customer segments.
- **Friendly-fraud labels are contested.** A 'consumer' dispute may reflect a genuinely confusing descriptor or cancellation flow; the right fix is often product-side, not a block.

## Maintenance

Retrain on a rolling window once new labels mature; re-run `cbp evaluate` to refresh this card and check calibration before changing any blocking threshold.
